text: Every BxAgents project can ship its own chat page. This is the web UI of an Acme support agent, built from one gateway file. It starts at sign in, with accounts you declare in code.
Signed in, you land in a clean chat. The header shows the agent, the model picker, and icon buttons for your conversations, notes, an API key and the theme. Hover any of them for its name.
Ask a question and the answer streams in as it is written, with Markdown formatting and lists.
The model picker lists the profiles the app chose to offer. Pick the planner profile, and the next answer comes from a different model, in the same conversation.
When the agent calls a tool, the page shows it as a block you can open, with the tool's name and what it was called with.

The ring in the header fills as the conversation grows. Click it for the breakdown: the system prompt, the tool definitions, the notes and the messages, each with its size, and a button to compact the conversation.
Type a slash for the commands. The menu lists each one with a hint, and the lightning button next to the message box opens it too.
Every conversation is saved. Start a new chat, and the old one stays in the list, ready to open again.
Notes keep what the agent should remember about you. Add one, and it is there next time.
Dark mode is one click, and the page remembers your choice.

That is the whole web UI: sign in, streaming answers, a model picker you control, tools, the context breakdown, commands, saved conversations, notes and themes. All from a few lines of YAML and one gateway file.
